newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Boeing ready to drop exclusive pacts - EU source.
newsitem.headline: Boeing ready to drop exclusive pacts - EU source.

text.p: Boeing Co has proposed scrapping its exclusive supply pacts with three airlines in an effort to win EU regulatory approval for its merger with McDonnell Douglas , a European Union source said.

The source gave no further details. The European Commission is expected to decide today whether to clear the $15 billion merger, which has led to political strains between the United States and the EU.
Boeing's exclusive supply pacts with AMR Corp's American Airlines, Continental Airlines and Delta Air Lines have been one of the major stumbling blocks in talks between the two sides.
Edith Cresson, the French commissioner in charge of research, hinted as she arrived for the Commission's weekly meeting that she would resist clearing the deal despite the last-minute offer.
"That doesn't change at all the heart of the problem," she told Reuters.
Another commissioner, Sweden's Anita Gradin, was more upbeat. "I'm sure," she said, when asked whether there would be a deal.
Other commissioners were more cautious. "I don't know, we will have to discuss it," Commission President Jacques Santer said.
The commissioners were expected to be briefed on Boeing's proposals, submitted by fax on Tuesday afternoon, before starting their regular weekly meeting at 0900/0700 GMT.
